backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/mfa.rs:591-803 — pub async fn disable_mfa accepts a TOTP code or recovery code and returns 400 INVALID_CODE on mismatch (line 700-709). No per-user rate limiter is invoked anywhere in the handler, unlike sibling verify_mfa_setup (line 329 calls setup_verify_attempt_allowed) and verify_recovery_code (line 1126 calls recovery_attempt_allowed). Repro: attacker with a valid access token calls POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/disable with incrementing 6-digit codes — ~10^6 unthrottled attempts suffice to disable MFA, a full MFA bypass on success. Mirror the setup_verify_attempt_allowed pattern (user-keyed LazyLock<UserRateLimiter> + reset on success) in disable_mfa.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/mfa.rs:912-1062 — pub async fn regenerate_backup_codes verifies a TOTP code (line 981-993) and rotates all recovery codes on success (line 1019-1032, regenerate_backup_codes_rls), invalidating the user's current codes. No per-user rate limiter is applied — asymmetric with verify_mfa_setup and verify_recovery_code in the same file. Repro: attacker with a stolen access token brute-forces the 6-digit TOTP against POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/backup-codes/regenerate; a hit both bypasses MFA (new codes under attacker control) AND locks the legitimate user out of their printed recovery codes. Apply the same per-user sliding-window throttle used by setup_verify_attempt_allowed.
